verdict.rationale: Vue's official FAQ answers 'What browsers does Vue support?' directly. Vue 3.x requires native ES2016 support, excludes IE11, and uses features that cannot be polyfilled, so legacy browser support means staying on Vue 2.x. That settles both the polyfill question and the drop-legacy decision. missing for 10: an explicit per-browser/version matrix (only an ES2016 baseline is stated), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I know the framework's officially supported browser matrix so I can plan polyfills or decide when to drop legacy support

citations.quote: The latest version of Vue (3.x) only supports browsers with native ES2016 support. This excludes IE11.
Vue 3.x uses ES2016 features that cannot be polyfilled in legacy browsers, so if you need to support legacy browsers, you will need to use Vue 2.x instead.
